newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk MP warns of govt challenge ahead of talks.
newsitem.headline: Turk MP warns of govt challenge ahead of talks.

text.p: A former minister from Turkey's Islamist-led coalition warned on Monday of efforts to bring down the shaky ruling alliance if his right-wing party did not support a new government formula set for discussion this week.
"If there is no resignation from the government, the government must be brought down with a confidence vote," former health minister Yildirim Aktuna from the True Path Party (DYP) told Reuters.

Aktuna and another DYP dissident, former trade and industry minister Yalim Erez, resigned their posts last month in protest at the reluctance of their Islamist coalition partners to support an army-led crackdown on religious activism.
Erez told Reuters he was to hold a second round of talks with opposition leaders this week on forming a government alliance excluding the Islamist Welfare Party of Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan.
He said he would meet on Tuesday or Wednesday with the leader of the main opposition Motherland Party, Mesut Yilmaz, and leftist leader Bulent Ecevit.
Aktuna said last week's talks had brought agreement on an alternative coalition including the DYP and this proposal would be put to the party leader Tansu Ciller this week.
"If there will not be a government which includes the whole of the DYP, a new government including some DYP members will be put on the agenda," he said.
The secularist military demanded curbs on Islamist activism at a meeting of the powerful National Security Council in February, but the 10-month-old coalition has yet to carry out its key demands.
